newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African industrials dragged to close by futures.
newsitem.headline: S.African industrials dragged to close by futures.

text.p: South African near-term industrial futures took a whack at the start of trade on Wednesday and struggled to regain composure throughout the day, dragging industrial shares down with them.

Futures players attempted to buoy very frail industrial share futures contracts by shedding the stocks and snatching the futures. While avoiding a slide, industrial shares floundered throughout the day to finish weak.
South African futures were knocked after the U.S. December Standard and Poor futures index was battered overnight and dealers said the smack must have come from the Australian or Eastern markets.
The soft South African market failed to find support in Wall Street's slight hop overnight as panic arising from negative sentiment entrenched itself.
Dealers said that world markets would be nervously eyeing Wall Street's open which was seen lower. By 1445 the Dow Jones industrial index had lost over one percent.
Gold shares on the other hand made a feeble start to the day as bullion slept, but as the metal price livened up to lift itself above $369 gold stocks inched up.
Overall, dealers said volumes were high.
The industrial index was 45.6 points off at 7,851.8, the all-shares lost 27.3 points to 6,639.1 and the golds inched up 15.4 points to 1,542.1.
